attempted_axis: Instrument a WebFrank refusal instead of recording it as a fact about the function (AGENTS.md discipline 14). The gauntworld fn_8005FB48 instruction_permutation pin aborted the whole TU build with `ValueError: instruction permutation relocation input hash changed` the moment ANY source edit landed anywhere in gauntworld.c, making the TU's 12 open functions unworkable. Established WHAT check fired, on WHICH word, and whether a sound-but-finer check would pass.

attributes.law_screen: AGENTS.md discipline 14 (a guard's refusal is a measurement of the guard) is the governing rule and it is what turned a build-stopping blocker into a five-minute diagnosis. claim.law.HA_relocations-ride-their-atom-into-the-proof-inputs-too-not-only-into-the-hashes.20260901.v1 SCREENED and is the nearest neighbour, but it is about relocations MOVING with their atom; this is about the stored hash binding an ELF symbol INDEX that has nothing to do with the window. claim.law.CH_sda21-relocation-offset-encoding-differs-between-our-objects-and-the-extracted-target.20260901.v1 and claim.law.HV_emb-sda21-relocation-offset-differs-between-our-objects-and-the-target.20260901.v1 SCREENED and NOT the mechanism: the offsets and types are identical on both sides here, only the symbol index moved. claim.GW_gauntworld-roster-census-artifact-split.20260901.v1's benign-relocation-naming rule APPLIED in spirit - the general form is 'check the DATA the symbol names, never the name or the number'. No law existed for this class; one is proposed alongside.
attributes.probed_form:
DIAGNOSIS. webfrank.py `_relocation_sha256` (line 978) hashes each relocation as `struct.pack('>IIi', offset, info, addend)`. ELF `r_info` embeds the SYMBOL TABLE INDEX in its high 24 bits. The stored `before_relocations_sha256` therefore asserts a TU-GLOBAL quantity, and any edit that adds or removes one symbol anywhere in the object renumbers every later index and trips the assertion on a window that did not change.

THE TRIGGER, measured. The fn_8005F0F4 fix makes the function need a sixth callee-saved FPR, so its prologue call changes `_savefpr_27` -> `_savefpr_26` (and `_restfpr_27` -> `_restfpr_26`). `_savefpr_26` was already referenced elsewhere in the TU and `_savefpr_27` then had no remaining referent, so the symbol table lost one entry and 67 relocation rows renumbered - visible in objdump -r as `@2202` -> `@2201` across the whole .text table.

THE DECISIVE EVIDENCE THAT THE WINDOW IS UNCHANGED. Comparing the pre-edit and post-edit body objects (build/GUNE5D/src/game/world/.postprocess/body/gauntworld.o) over fn_8005FB48's +0x74..+0x8c window:
  window TEXT before_sha256  4b6541e8... IDENTICAL on both
  window TEXT after_sha256   e2bf5e78... IDENTICAL on both
  +0x02 type 109 addend 0 name 'sZeroDouble'  sym index 339 -> 341
  +0x0a type 109 addend 0 name 'sItemZero'    sym index 337 -> 339
  +0x12 type 109 addend 0 name '@1280'        sym index  43 ->  43
Same count, same offsets, same relocation TYPE, same addends, same symbol NAMES. The pin's own text hashes both still match, `check_permutation_dependences` passes, and the name-based `verify_relocation_binding` against the target's relocations is unaffected - it is keyed on names, not indices.

RESOLUTION TAKEN. The two relocation hashes in config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json's gauntworld entry were re-stamped (before 9b5e64d9..., after f7810802...) inside commit da098cc62. Nothing else in the rule changed: order, window bounds, text hashes, copy_register_fields and the whole audit block are byte-identical. The re-stamp was produced by a fail-closed script (GW_scratch/restamp_apply.py, deliberately NOT promoted - see below) that refuses unless BOTH stored text hashes still match AND every window relocation still carries the same (offset, type, addend, symbol NAME) as the authoring derivation.
attributes.residual:
RECLASSIFIED, not closed. The immediate blocker is cleared and fn_8005FB48 re-verifies byte-exact, but the underlying fragility stands and will re-fire on the next gauntworld edit that perturbs the symbol table.

THE FIX THIS RECORD RECOMMENDS, for whoever owns webfrank (WF this run): make the stored relocation hash bind (offset, r_type, addend, symbol NAME) instead of raw `info`. That is the quantity the rule's own prose says it means to pin - its mechanism text derives the permutation order 'under an explicit symbol correspondence' by NAME - and it is stable under unrelated TU edits. The change invalidates every stored relocation hash image-wide, so it needs a one-off re-stamp pass over webfrank.json, which is why it is proposed rather than done by this lane.

UNTIL THEN, the working procedure for any lane editing a TU that carries an instruction_permutation pin: expect the refusal on your first build, do NOT treat it as a fact about your edit, dump the window's relocations by NAME on both objects, and re-stamp only if the text hashes and every symbol name/type/addend are unchanged. If any NAME differs, the refusal is real and the edit must be re-examined.
attributes.scope: config/GUNE5D/webfrank.json, two hash strings in the game/world/gauntworld entry, committed inside da098cc62 as a forced co-change. No webfrank.py change, no rule mechanism change, no new rule, no guard weakened - every executable check the pin performs still runs unmodified.
attributes.verification: fndiff --clean on the pinned function after the re-stamp: '== fn_8005FB48: MATCH (pool-name noise only), 0 real diff lines (+2 pool-name lines suppressed)'. regnorm TU census after: fn_8005FB48 '165 paired, 0 renaming, 0 STRUCTURAL, 0 unpaired -> EXACT'. defake_gate.py check over the whole TU: GATE OK, no sibling regression. Full `ninja -j2` green with `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK` on every commit that followed. The before/after relocation tables and both text hashes were dumped with webfrank.py's own `_sections`/`_symbols`/`_function_text_relocations`/`_relocation_sha256` helpers, not a hand-rolled ELF reader, so the numbers are the ones the guard itself would compute.
